facts.fact: Titanic sank two hours and forty minutes after hitting an iceberg on 14 April 1912, resulting in around 1,500 deaths.
Passengers felt a shudder or bump during the collision, with some describing it as "a thousand marbles".
Water poured into the ship at 7 long tons per second, faster than it could be pumped out.
Titanic had 20 lifeboats, accommodating 1,178 people, barely half the passengers and crew.
Water at −2 °C (28 °F) caused most victims to die within 15–30 minutes from cold shock or hypothermia.
Collapsible lifeboats were difficult to launch, requiring manual handling from the officers' quarters.
Cold shock caused 20% of victims to die within two minutes, while 50% died within 15–30 minutes.
The ship's design could not handle six flooded compartments, leading to inevitable sinking.
Lifeboats were launched starting at 00:05, but many were not fully loaded due to panic and confusion.
Titanic's speed of 22 knots (41 km/h) in ice-heavy waters was later criticized as reckless.

sentences.text: What would it feel like to be on the Titanic as it sank?
You feel a sudden shudder as the ship hits an iceberg, followed by icy water flooding lower decks.
Lifeboats were scarce, with only 1,178 seats for the people aboard.
The ship listed about five degrees to starboard and two degrees down by the head, and water at -2°C could kill in 15–30 minutes.
Cold shock and hypothermia set in quickly, with most drowning or succumbing within 15–30 minutes.
What factors influenced survival on the Titanic?

title: What If You Were on the Sinking Titanic?
